learned_rules:
- **The money shape rates 8, or 9 if the radar shows the story still climbing and mcap is under ~$1M.** It looks like this: a MIGRATED coin leading on 5m volume, 25–45% off its local high, a printed higher low above the hourly low, 5m flow at or above the hourly pace, more buys than sells, top 10 under 15%, low RugCheck bundles. Both real winners looked like this (CATBOT 4.44x, FLOATER 2.19x, both under $1M) (V1, V6, V13). Rate it what it earns so code sizes it up (owner goal).
- **Owner floor: 7 under ~$1M mcap.** If the hard lines pass, flow is live (5m ≥ $10k and at or above pace), a higher low is printed and the first resistance is ≥1.5x away, rate it 7 or higher. Don't dock points for things the checklist already measured.
- **The MIGRATED buy zone is 10–60% off the local high** (owner rule). Within 10% of the high is a PASS, blocker "chasing" (42 skips: 3 ran, 36 dumped).
- **The shallow band (10–25% off the high) is a breakout trade, capped at 7.** It must be the 5m volume leader, pushing into the high right now, with flow at or above pace. Otherwise PASS, blocker "no breakout".
- **A spike counts as chasing anywhere in the zone.** If the last 5m candle is up more than 25% or 5m volume is more than 3x the hourly pace, wait for a retrace and a printed higher low. Blocker "chasing spike" (PILLSEY).
- **On MIGRATED, flow below pace or no printed higher low is a PASS, never a probe.** A printed higher low means three things: a bounce off the hourly low, a pullback that holds above it, and price back above that bounce's high. A buy share, a fib touch or a first green candle is not one. Blockers "flow below pace" / "no higher low" (Slingoor, ANAKIN, BLUE, SI, AAPLCAT never got past 1.01x).
- **Buy close to the structure.** Enter only within ~12% above the printed higher low, so the thesis breaks before the hard stop. Further above it is a mid-range entry: wait for a pullback or PASS, blocker "mid-range". Stops fill around −30 to −38%, not −20%, so entry distance is the real risk control.
- **Rate on the first resistance (prior high, POC or 0.618).** At ≥1.5x away it can rate 8–9. At 1.3–1.5x the cap is 7. Under 1.3x is a PASS, blocker "target too close" (PAWCAT, SWAN).
- **Above ~$1M mcap, a probe (6) is the most you take.** Only take it if the first resistance is ≥1.5x away and a breakout with flow at or above pace is printing right now. Otherwise PASS, blocker "big cap, no room" (1 green in 10).
- **A migration under 1h old that is still bleeding off its bond spike waits for a base above the hourly low.** Blocker "too new" (50 skips: 9 ran, 41 dumped).
- **In a vamp field, buy only the leader by 5m volume and radar mentions.** A bundle cluster inside a big same-ticker field is a PASS, blocker "split crowd" (V1, V3).
- **A DIP needs all of these:** a 40–70% drawdown, 5m flow at least 0.7x the hourly pace (owner gate, no "rising" needed), the story still on the radar, and a printed higher low with entry within ~12% of it. If all pass, size by conviction (7–8 when clean). A DIP whose catalyst already printed (news, rebrand) is a probe (6) at most until it reclaims its pullback high. A thin tech/LARP story is a PASS, blocker "dead story" (HEXN x2, SIS; DIPs 0 for 5).
- **Hard blocks:** top 10 over 25%, dev over 1%, bundles or insiders over the line, mint or freeze authority live, LP not burned, a political figure, RugCheck danger, any hack/exploit/drain story (V6, V13, V17, owner). Name the blocker in every PASS.
- **If RugCheck didn't load, it's a probe at most (6), not a block.** That needs the dossier's top-10 and dev numbers clean, mcap under $1M and the rest in the money shape. Say bundles are unverified.
- **Manage the trade; stops sell with no review.** If the printed higher low breaks, sell. If it hasn't reached 1.05x by minute 10 with flow under pace, exit. If it's green before initials and 5m volume drops under half the hourly pace, sell half. At the time stop, exit; the only extension is one 15-minute window while a volume surge at or above pace is printing. Re-enter a stopped-out coin only once, and only when it reclaims its prior high with flow at or above pace (re-entries 0 for 4).

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing has a positive after-cost edge. All 98 settled coins average -15.7% net under the simple plan, and every setup and stage is negative: MIGRATED -13.6% (n=70), FINAL_STRETCH -20.0% (n=14), DIP -21.7% (n=14). The main reason is the 9.5% average round-trip cost on a $10 buy. With a +50%/-20% bracket and that cost, a coin nets about +40% when it runs and about -30% when it dumps, so the plan breaks even only if roughly 42% of coins run. The observed rate is 16.3% (95% CI about 9–24%), so the overall verdict is solid even at n=98. The per-setup splits are not: n=14 gives about ±19 points, and coins from the same day and meta move together. I can't answer whether the routine model's would-buys beat its passes because it made zero would-buys. It declined all 49 coins it reviewed, including all 5 of the day's 4.5–5.5x runners. Even so, declining was right on average, since that reviewed group nets -16.2% under the simple plan.
findings: Costs are bigger than the price edge. Average cost is 9.5% per round trip, and the gross result before costs is only about -6%. At this size, even a coin-flip entry would bleed about 10% a trade. This matches the paper trades: $18.83 of the $25.79 loss was fees and slippage.
MIGRATED is the least bad setup: n=70, 18.6% ran, 20.0% hit 2x, net -13.6%. It still needs about 2.3x its current run rate to break even.
DIP is the worst setup: n=14, 7.1% ran (1 coin), 0% hit 2x, 78.6% dumped, net -21.7%. Not one dip buy produced a 2x in 24h. That fits 'a dip with fading volume is a falling knife', but n=14 is small.

FINAL_STRETCH: n=14, 28.6% hit 2x (4 coins) but only 14.3% ran (2 coins), net -20.0%. Half the coins that eventually doubled hit -20% before +50%. That looks like the V1 pre-bond dump shaking out a tight stop. Too few samples to act on alone.
Overall, 18.4% of coins hit 2x but only 16.3% ran under the bracket. Some later winners dipped through -20% first, so the -20% stop is clipping part of the right tail.

Brain-reviewed coins (n=49) have a fat right tail: 28.6% hit 2x, against 8.3% for checklist failures (n=48). They are also more violent: 79.6% dumped vs 68.8%, so net is slightly worse (-16.2% vs -14.8%). The checklist is mostly filtering volatility, not expected value. Under the 1.5x/-20% plan, the extra upside gets cancelled by extra stop-outs.

All 5 top runners (BANDANA 5.52x, Mandy 5.50x, Bust 4.81x, PAY 4.52x, SBS 4.46x) were brain-declined. All were young (0.02–0.77h) and small ($14k–$56k mcap). Two (Mandy and PAY) peaked within 10–12 minutes, which is too fast for a data feed that runs seconds behind. This is a list of the best outcomes only. We don't have the base rate for young, small coins, which mostly dumped.

These skip rules are earning their keep: top 10 over 25% blocked 32 coins, 0 ran, 30 dumped. 'Falling knife (code)' blocked 19, 0 ran, 18 dumped. Thin 5m volume blocked 11, 0 ran. 'Bundles over the line' blocked 10, 0 ran. 'Too new / sniping' blocked 19, 1 ran. RugCheck danger blocked 21, 3 ran (CAP 2.6x), and its 18 dumps include GTASZN at 0.03x and PCVI at 0.02x, which look like real rugs.

The only skip rule with a run rate above the 16% base is 'flow below pace': 23 blocked, 7 ran (30%), 15 dumped. Its ran examples peaked at just 1.51–1.77x, though. A rough bracket estimate is 7×40.5 − 15×29.5 ≈ -7% per coin after costs, so loosening it would still lose money.
'Near the high / chasing' blocked 17: 4 ran (23.5%, BEAR 2.32x and STICK 2.08x), 13 dumped, roughly -13% net. Keep it.

Vamp clustering is going undetected. FIONA shows up under 4 different contract addresses (blocked for flow, bundles, no higher low and LARP), and every one dumped, one to 0.04x. LOOSY, AI and SI each show up under 2 addresses. The vamp/copycat rule itself fired only 3 times.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: skip when the estimated round-trip cost is above about 5%. Also re-run the whole week at $25 and $50 sizes to see how much of the 9.5% is fixed (priority fee, bribe) versus slippage. If the fixed part dominates, size is the biggest lever and no entry rule fixes it.

Exit variant: re-score every setup with stop -35% instead of -20%, sell initials at 2x, trail the rest by 30% from peak, and a 60-minute time stop. Test it first on brain-reviewed coins (n=49 today, 28.6% hit 2x) to see whether the right tail pays for the wider stop after costs.

Young small-cap bucket: setup in {FINAL_STRETCH, MIGRATED}, age ≤ 1h, mcap $14k–$60k, checklist passed. Report n, ran %, 2x % and net for the whole bucket, not just the winners. Only consider it if net beats 0 with n ≥ 50 across at least 4 different days.

Turn DIP off for evaluation unless a narrower version proves itself: DIP with 5m volume ≥ 1h pace, buy ratio ≥ 0.55 and drawdown 40–60%. It needs net > 0 on at least 30 week samples. Otherwise drop DIP.
FINAL_STRETCH stop test: bracket +100%/-35% against +50%/-20%, to check whether the pre-bond dump is what's stopping out the eventual 2x coins.
Loosen 'flow below pace' only as a shadow test: flow ratio 0.5–1.0 (just below the current pace) with checklist passed. Adopt only if week net after costs is above 0. Today's estimate is about -7%.

Vamp cluster rule: if the normalized symbol (lowercased and trimmed) matches 2 or more contract addresses seen in the last 6h, allow only the one with the highest mcap and 5m volume, and only if it was first-seen earliest. Check how many of the FIONA, LOOSY, AI and SI variants it would have blocked.
Holder tightening test: among checklist-passed coins, compare net for top 10 at 15–25% against under 15% (V6). Only tighten to 15% if the 15–25% band is clearly worse.
data_issues: would_buy n=0, so the main question (did the would-buys beat the passes?) can't be answered. Check whether watch-only mode suppresses BUY verdicts or stops logging them, or whether the brain really said PASS 49 times out of 49. If it's real, the brain is too conservative to evaluate at all. Logging the brain's conviction score and its counterfactual size on every call would make passes testable.
The label 'brain_passed' is ambiguous. The top runners show brain='PASS', which means the brain declined them. Rename it brain_declined so nobody reads it as 'passed the brain gate'.

Pacing gap: in 48h there were 262 brain calls, 19 plan-limit hits and 100 candidates skipped with no brain. The 24h stats show only 1 'not_researched' coin and the 'brain paced' bucket has only 2. Most coins skipped for lack of a brain call seem not to be followed, so the sample has a blind spot of about 100 coins. Follow them all.

SBS conflicts across sections: the top-runners list says 4.46x, but the 'fees or size' skip bucket says best_x 1.59. Either the windows differ (6h vs first-touch) or two log rows for the same coin disagree.

SBS is tagged MIGRATED with age 0.019h (about 68 seconds). For migrated tokens, age seems to be measured from pool creation, not token creation. That breaks the 'too new' and 'age ≤ 12h' logic. Log both ages.

Skip buckets overlap and use a different window. The 48h skips total 180 bucket entries, and coins appear in several buckets (LOOSY HF2R… is in 3, ANTS and GATO in 2 each). They are 48h figures while everything else is 24h. Log the primary blocker separately from all blockers.

In the skip tables, ran examples show worst_x=1.0 and dumped examples often best_x=1.0. That suggests tracking stops at the first barrier touched, which means exit variants (wider stops, 2x initials, trailing) can't be tested from skip rows. Store the full 6h price path, or at least max_x, min_x and the order they happened, for every coin.

We don't know the sampling interval. Mandy and PAY peaked in 10–12 minutes, and the 'both crossed between samples, count the loss' rule depends on how often prices are sampled. Log the interval, and record fills at the next sample plus latency instead of at the logged price.
This summary has no 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio, drawdown or cost-per-coin fields. Rule ideas need per-coin rows with these fields, plus the round-trip cost split into fixed and slippage.
Symbols have stray whitespace ('Gino ', 'apocry '). Normalize them before any vamp or duplicate matching.
Effective sample size is smaller than n because coins cluster by day and meta. Report results by calendar day, so one hot meta can't drive the week's conclusion.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing has a positive edge after costs. All 166 settled coins averaged -11.3% net under the simple plan, and no setup or stage was positive. The closest were FINAL_STRETCH at -3.3% (n=21) and DIP at -5.9% (n=20). Both look slightly positive before costs (about +6.7% and +3.6%), but with ~20 samples the error bar is roughly ±13 points, and some coins are logged more than once, so both are noise for now. The biggest loss is the 9.8% average round-trip cost on a $10 buy: at that cost, the simple plan only breaks even if about 43% of coins hit 1.5x before -20%. Overall only 23.5% did, and the best setup (FINAL_STRETCH) managed 38.1%. I can't answer whether the routine model's would-buys beat its passes, because it logged zero would-buys in 24h out of 99 coins it reviewed. The coins it passed on did lose more than the coins the checklist rejected (-15.2% vs -5.7%). That suggests passing them was correct, but also that clearing the checklist didn't pick better coins this day.
findings: Costs decide everything. The 'ran' and 'dumped' shares reproduce avg_net almost exactly: 0.235×50 − 0.669×20 − 9.8 ≈ -11.3. So the plan is effectively a race between +50% and -20%. Breakeven needs ~42.6% ran at 9.8% cost, but only ~35.7% at 5% cost and ~31% at 3%.
MIGRATED is the bulk and the worst: n=125, 20.8% ran, 71.2% dumped, net -13.5%. Before costs it is still about -3.7%, so this setup has no raw edge as currently filtered.

FINAL_STRETCH has the highest hit rate: n=21, 38.1% ran, net -3.3%. But only 14.3% reached 2x, so most of its runners stalled between 1.5x and 2x. That fits the guide's pre-bond dump and stall pattern (V1) and supports taking profit early on this setup. At a ~5% cost it would be about +1.4%, which still isn't significant at n=21.
DIP: n=20, 25% ran, but only 45% dumped (lowest of any setup). Net -5.9%, about +3.6% before costs. Losses were less frequent, not wins more frequent.

MIGRATED runners mostly kept going: 17.6% of coins hit 2x against 20.8% that hit 1.5x, so ~85% of those reaching 1.5x also reached 2x. For this setup the 1.5x exit may cut winners short. Small sample, but worth testing an exit at 2x for initials (V2, V11).

Stages: checklist_failed n=67, 29.9% ran, -5.7%. brain_passed n=99, 19.2% ran, 75.8% dumped, -15.2%. The ~9.5-point gap is about 2 standard errors, and the samples aren't independent, so treat it as a hint. It does mean coins that cleared the checklist didn't do better on this day.

The hard-line skip filters are earning their keep against the 23.5% base ran rate. Top 10 over 25%: 21 blocked, 1 ran, 19 dumped. Flow below pace: 31 blocked, 4 ran, 24 dumped. Near the high / chasing: 22 blocked, 4 ran, 17 dumped. RugCheck danger: 17 blocked, 3 ran, 14 dumped. Too new / sniping: 18 blocked, 2 ran, 15 dumped.

One filter looks too tight. 'Falling knife / no higher low' blocked 9 coins: 2 ran (UrAnus best 2.97x), only 2 dumped, 3 flat, 2 pending. It's the only skip reason where dumps don't dominate, but n=9 is far too small to loosen it yet.

The biggest runners were very young MIGRATED or DIP coins: RIZZMAS3 at 0.16h age and $42k mcap (8.07x in 50 min), snowball at 0.5–2h and $75–85k (6.4–7.5x), UrAnus at 0.87h and $98k (5.4x in 30 min). Under the simple plan each of these counts as just +50% minus costs, so the reported numbers say nothing about a trailing-runner exit.
Brain capacity is fine: 264 brain calls in 48h, 0 plan-limit hits, 0 candidates skipped for lack of a brain. Pacing is not what's holding results back.
rule_ideas: Cost gate, to apply before any other rule: skip if est_round_trip_cost_pct > 5% at the intended size. Also re-run every bucket at $25, $50 and $100 sizes to see whether any setup turns positive once costs drop. The current $10 'probe' is not a size where fees work.

FINAL_STRETCH, checklist passed, 5m volume ≥ $10k, buy ratio ≥ 0.55. Exit at 1.5x or -20%, plus a time stop if it stalls under bond. Success bar: ran% ≥ breakeven at the actual logged cost, with n ≥ 50 unique coins.
MIGRATED exit variant: sell initials at 2x, trail the rest at -30% from the peak, hard stop -20%. Compare net% against the 1.5x simple plan on the same coins.

MIGRATED, age 0.5–3h, mcap $40k–$150k, 5m volume ≥ $10k, flow ratio ≥ 1 (5m volume at or above its hourly pace). Versus MIGRATED with age over 3h. Tests whether this day's young runners are a pattern or a few outliers.
Exclude MIGRATED where age > 12h and mcap is under $70k (outside both guide windows, V1 and V6). Report them separately so old revived coins like HODL don't mix with fresh migrations.

DIP, drawdown 40–70% from the 6h high, 5m volume ≥ 0.5× the hourly pace, buy ratio ≥ 0.55, checklist passed. Version (a) requires a higher low, version (b) doesn't. Loosen the 'no higher low' block only if (b) beats (a) on n ≥ 30.
Brain value test: log a shadow conviction score (1–10) on every brain PASS. Check whether net% rises with conviction. If it doesn't, the brain adds no ranking signal beyond the code filters.
Keep top10 > 25%, flow below pace, near-high and RugCheck danger as blocks. Re-check them weekly: loosen any whose blocked ran% climbs above the overall base rate on n ≥ 30.
data_issues: Zero would-buys (stage would_buy n=0) across 99 brain reviews. Either the model never says buy in watch-only mode, or the would-buy decision isn't logged. Either way the main question (did its picks beat its passes?) can't be answered. Fix before the next review.

The same coin is logged more than once: snowball appears twice in top_runners at different stages, mcaps and ages. STREETS is in 3 skip buckets; Trader, LOOSY and CATPOOP in 2 each; RIZZMAS3 in top_runners and in a skip bucket. This inflates n and makes samples correlated. Deduplicate to the first entry per contract address per 6h window.

Peak numbers disagree for the same coin: RIZZMAS3 shows max_x 8.07 in top_runners but best_x 1.84 in skips. UrAnus shows 5.41 vs 2.97. The two may use different entry points, windows, or wick vs sampled price. Pick one definition.

HODL is 13,179h old (~1.5 years) yet tagged MIGRATED with a 7.9x move. Check that the setup classification and price feed are right, and that the move isn't a thin-pool wick that couldn't actually be traded.
RIZZMAS3 was 0.16h old when logged as MIGRATED, while a separate 'too new / sniping' block exists. The age cutoff seems to be applied inconsistently.
'Brain paced' blocked 6 coins, but routine_brain_usage reports candidates_skipped_no_brain = 0 and plan_limit_hits = 0. One of these counters is wrong, or the self-imposed pace cap isn't counted.
The skips_48h buckets add up to exactly 166, the same as the 24h settled count. Probably a coincidence, but check that the 48h window label is right and how pending coins are counted.

The payload doesn't define 'ran', 'dumped' and 'flat'. The math implies first touch of 1.5x vs -20%, but the sampling interval and the both-crossed rule (counted as a loss) should be stated and logged.
Costs are estimated only for a $10 buy. Log pool liquidity and cost at several sizes, since costs were $18.83 of the $25.79 real loss.

top_runners lists only winners and leaves out 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio and drawdown. That's survivorship bias, and the fields needed to test the rules above are missing. Export the full per-coin rows.

Timeline: the watch-only week was set for Nov 3–10, but today is Nov 22 and it's still running. Confirm the Nov 10 review happened, or that the extension was intended. Twelve extra days of data is fine, but it should be on purpose.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing has a positive after-cost edge yet. All 229 settled coins average -8.7% net on the simple plan. Before costs they average about +0.9%, so the 9.6% average round-trip cost on a $10 buy accounts for the whole loss. That is the same story as the 22 paper trades, where fees and slippage were $18.83 of the $25.79 lost. The best setup is FINAL_STRETCH: n=39, 35.9% hit 1.5x, -4.9% net. With a 1.5x target, a -20% stop and about 10% costs, a setup needs roughly 43% hitting the target to break even. At n=39 the hit rate's 95% range is about 21–51%, so this sample can't separate it from MIGRATED, from coin-flip noise or from breakeven. I can't say whether the routine model's would-buys beat its passes, because it made zero would-buys in 24h. The coins it passed on (n=157, -8.4%) did slightly better than the coins the checklist failed (n=70, -9.8%), but both lost money. Passing everything was the right call on average. One process note: the watch-only review was set for about Nov 10 and today is Nov 23, so the owner should decide whether this is still the plan.
findings: All coins (n=229): 25.8% ran, 59.4% dumped, median peak 1.25x, 11.8% hit 2x, -8.7% net after 9.6% cost. Before costs that is about +0.9%: no edge, just a cost drag.
MIGRATED (n=162) is the weakest setup and 71% of the sample: 23.5% ran, 62.3% dumped, -10.0% net (about +0.5% before costs). The simple plan has nothing to work with here.

FINAL_STRETCH (n=39) is the least bad: 35.9% ran, 20.5% hit 2x, median peak 1.44x, -4.9% net (about +5.1% before costs). That gap is about 1 standard error (roughly 5 points). Ran plus dumped is 100%, so every one of these coins resolved within 6h; it is a coin-flip-style distribution.
DIP (n=28) dumps least (35.7%) but barely moves: median peak 1.08x, 3.6% hit 2x, 39% flat, -6.8% net. Dips mostly go sideways and then pay the fee.

The routine model's rejections (brain_passed n=157, -8.4%) and checklist failures (n=70, -9.8%) differ by 1.4 points. That is noise. Neither the checklist nor the routine model splits winners from losers on this metric, though both correctly kept money out of a losing pool.

The top runners (Fly 22.9x, MINELIUS 14.7x, Hedge 10.0x, FSDV15 9.2x) were all 0.09–0.24h old and all failed the checklist. FOAM (6.0x) was 0.04h old and the routine model passed on it. In the same 48h, 32 'too new / sniping' blocks went 7 ran, 25 dumped (78% dumped). The big runners are survivors from a pool that mostly dies.
These skip rules are earning their keep (48h, mostly dumps): too new 25/32 dumped, flow below pace 23/30, near the high 20/25, RugCheck danger 14/16 (several to 0.01–0.03x), top 10 over 25% 13/17.

The weakest skip reason is the routine model's 'falling knife / no higher low' (n=16): 4 ran, 4 dumped, 5 flat, 3 pending. Before costs that is about +9% on the simple plan, about -1% after costs. It overlaps with 'falling knife (code)' and 'brain paced' (STREETS appears in all three), so the real sample is smaller than it looks.
Under the simple plan, each skip category's return after costs is 0% or worse except 'other' (n=6). No rule is clearly blocking profitable coins at $10 size.
Brain capacity is fine: 397 calls in 48h, 0 plan-limit hits, 0 stop reviews or candidates without a brain call.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: only count coins whose logged round-trip cost is at most 5% at the intended size. Then check whether the before-cost return of the deeper-pool coins survives. If costs are mostly fixed fees, rerun the whole week at $25 and $50 buys. Costs are the single biggest lever in this data.

FINAL_STRETCH, checklist passed, 5m volume of at least $10k, buy ratio of at least 0.55 (V1). Test whether at least 43% hit 1.5x before -20% on deduplicated coins. Below about 40% on the week's sample, drop it.

FINAL_STRETCH exit variant: sell enough at 2x to get the cost back, trail the rest, stop at -30% to survive the pre-bond dump (V1). Compare with the 1.5x/-20% plan on the same coins. 20.5% hit 2x, and the 1.5x cap cuts off exactly the tail the strategy depends on.

MIGRATED split by age (under 1h vs 1–12h) and mcap ($30–70k vs $70k–$11M, V6), with 5m volume of at least $10k and flow ratio (5m volume over hourly pace) of at least 1.0. Keep MIGRATED only if one cell is positive after costs with n of at least 40. Otherwise drop the setup.
DIP split by drawdown (40–55% vs 55–75%) with flow ratio of at least 1.0 and buy ratio of at least 0.55. Check whether the deeper or the shallower dips are the flat, fee-paying ones.

Test against the population, not anecdotes: compare deduplicated coins blocked by the routine model's 'falling knife / no higher low' with coins it passed for other reasons. If blocked coins do as well or better at n of at least 30, remove that subjective reason and keep the code version.
Ranking test: among coins the routine model scored, do the top 25% by conviction beat the bottom 25% after costs? If not, its conviction number carries no information and sizing by it is cosmetic.

Keep the 'too new' rule. Run one check on first sighting under 0.25h old: ran% vs dumped% after deduplication and after fixing the price spikes. The tiny-age runners are probably survivorship, and the hard line says don't snipe.
data_issues: would_buy is 0 out of 157 routine-model evaluations in 24h. Either it never says BUY or watch-only mode suppresses the verdict. Without hypothetical BUYs (and conviction), the week can't test the routine model's selection, which was the point. Log the verdict it would have given.

Peak multiples disagree for the same contract: Fly is 22.89x in top_runners vs best 1.52x in skips, MINELIUS 14.73x vs 1.53x, FOAM 6.00x vs 1.98x. Either each sighting uses its own reference price, or the max_x samples are outliers. Fly going 22.9x from $14.8k in 5.7 min at 0.24h old looks like a price jump at bond/migration or a wrong-pool quote. Validate before trusting any max_x or top_runner.

Setup labels look wrong: Fly (84tAc…cAc) and MCAT (BzPy…WMi) don't end in 'pump', yet Fly is labeled FINAL_STRETCH, which implies a pump.fun bonding curve. Check how the launchpad and setup are assigned.

There is double-counting: MINELIUS shows up in 3 skip categories, STREETS in 3, OpenIndex in 2. Different contracts share symbols (FSDV15, MCAT, SANTA ×2), which are probably vamps. Deduplicate by contract and give each coin one primary skip reason before the week's review.

Skip-reason coverage is incomplete: the categories add up to 195 blocks in 48h, while 24h alone has 227 rejected coins (70 checklist failures + 157 routine-model passes). Most rejections don't have a logged reason.
'brain paced' shows 11 blocks, but routine_brain_usage reports 0 candidates skipped for lack of a brain call. One of them is wrong, or 'paced' means something undocumented.
Stage counts add up to 228 (70+157+0+1), but n is 229. One coin has no stage. The one not_researched coin also has no stated reason.

Some skip best_x values cluster right at 3.0 (3.0, 2.97, 2.96). Check whether there's a cap. Some worst_x values are exactly 0.0 (FSDV15 3P7F…, BIGFOOT). Confirm those are real rugs, not a missing-price sentinel.
The windows are mixed: setup and stage stats cover 24h, skip stats cover 48h. They can't be cross-checked directly.
The cost model is only computed for a $10 buy. Log the split between fixed costs (priority fee, bribe) and slippage, so other sizes can be evaluated without re-collecting data.
